title: Kept conversation (opt-in, D-01b)
description: Draft 3.3 (gate 1, D-01b + D-01b'). The ONLY conversation content that outlives 'סיום', and only when the user ticked the unticked keep box (consent scope keep_for_improvement) AND keepOfferEligible(case) was true on the server at DELETE time. Store intake-kept, key k/<purge day>/<kept_id>, encrypted with its own key (INTAKE_KEPT_KEY, not derived from INTAKE_MASTER_SECRET). No linking ids: no session_id, lead_id, lead_ref, metrics_id, cookie, IP or user agent; per-turn timestamps are dropped. User text is the already identifier-masked text (SEC-07) after a second pass of name masking (reasonable effort); masking that did not complete means nothing is written (fail-safe), so name_mask.status can only be 'complete'. Draft 3.4 (SEC5-11): dates only, consented_on and purge_on = consented_on + 180 days; the hourly job deletes it (purge_failed heartbeat); a viewer read on or after purge_on deletes it on the spot. A reader may also delete it earlier (SEC5-05, logged first). User messages in a case are at most 800 characters (longer text gets meta.too_long and is never stored, ARCHITECTURE §6.1), so the 3000-character turn limit is not reached by real text; if it were, the write fails this schema and ends as store_failed (fail-safe, never a silent cut). No withdrawal code (D-01b': accepted risk, chosen by Eliya against the security recommendation). Read only through intake-kept-viewer (2FA, access log, no export); never by a model or an AI assistant. Never written for WhatsApp in v1, after any red flag, after a routing stop, or after a lead was sent.

kept_id.description: Random (128 bit), generated at keep time. Appears only here, in the store key, in the keep consent record and in the viewer's access log.

consent_record_id.description: record_id of the keep_for_improvement consent record (which has no session_id).

consented_on.description: Draft 3.4 (SEC5-11): the DAY of the keep consent only (UTC), so the record cannot be matched to infrastructure logs (Cloudflare, Netlify) by the second. The 180-day clock starts on this day (D-01b).

purge_on.description: consented_on + 180 days, a code constant (the consent text promises 'up to 6 months'). The hourly job deletes the record on this day (purge_failed heartbeat). Checked by unit test, not by this schema.

channel.description: v1: web only. WhatsApp keeps a phone number as its identity; keeping there is a phase-6 decision.

relation.description: keep_relation as computed by keepOfferEligible: self_adult = core_relation self and self_declared_minor not true; parent_of_child = core_relation child, reporter_role parent and subject_minor TRUE. Nobody else may be offered the box (legal: one cannot consent for another adult).

outcome.description: Always 1-4: the box is offered only on S5 (UX draft 4.4), and never after a red flag (outcome 5).

masked_identifiers.description: SEC-07 masking replaced an ID, phone or email in some message (the text below is the masked text).

status.description: Fail-safe: any other result (pattern over budget, engine error, exception) means the conversation is NOT kept (keep_result mask_failed).

ruleset.description: Version of the name-masking rules and lexicon (engine/keep).

name_mask.description: Reasonable effort only: common-word names (e.g. חיים, שמחה), institutions and rare details are not caught, which is why the opt-in text says 'we will try to remove names' (security, legal Q34).

slots.description: Final slot states. Quote values went through the same name masking. No evidence spans, no history.

turns.description: The conversation in order, without timestamps. Assistant fixed texts are kept as (id, version) only; their wording is in git.

text.description: user: the masked message. assistant: only a generated or template summary (origin generated / template_fallback), also name-masked.

allOf.description: A user turn is a message or a tap, never a fixed text.
An assistant turn always has an origin; fixed and FAQ texts are kept as references only, never as copied wording.

accessLogEntry.description: One line of the viewer's append-only access log (store intake-kept-log, key a/<YYYY-MM>/<entry_id>, 24 months). Content-free: who, when, what action, which kept_id. Written BEFORE the viewer returns any content; a failed log write means the content is not shown.

reader.description: D-01b: only Eliya and Hadas read kept conversations. No service account, no model, no AI assistant. Draft 3.4 (SEC5-10): 'unknown' records an attempt with an unrecognised user name (login_failed only). No raw IP is stored.

action.description: Draft 3.4: locked = an attempt refused during the 15-minute lockout after 5 failures (SEC5-06); delete = a reader deleted a kept conversation before its purge day (SEC5-05), logged BEFORE the deletion, with a closed-list reason.

second_factor.description: 2FA (SEC-24) on every session; content is served only after totp_ok. not_reached (draft 3.4, SEC5-10): the attempt failed before the TOTP step (unknown user, wrong password, lockout).

reason.description: Draft 3.4 (SEC5-05): delete only. identifiable = masking missed identifying details; disclosure = a disclosure the flags did not catch (legal Q23); request = a deletion request recognised by its content via privacy_contact; other.

allOf.description: SEC5-05 (draft 3.4): a delete names the record and the reason, by a known reader, after TOTP.
SEC5-05 (draft 3.4): a reason only on a delete.
SEC5-10 (draft 3.4): an unknown reader can only be a failed login that never reached TOTP.
SEC5-10 (draft 3.4): not_reached only on a failed or locked login.
